Topic: Rule of thumb: don't use Wald near boundaries
Story (story.md): Slow embarrassment that textbooks still teach Wald because it's easiest by hand; modern software defaults to Wilson or Clopper-Pearson.
Technical (chapter.md): Loop B Rule of thumb: Wald unreliable when N·p̂<5 or N·(1-p̂)<5, degenerate at p̂=0 or 1. Wilson is the default; Clopper-Pearson is safe but wide; Bayesian flat prior sits between; Jeffreys Beta(0.5,0.5) matches Clopper-Pearson (forward-ref Ch 6).

Story (story.md): Pollster paradox: "the true vote share is in [50,56] with probability 95%" is NOT what a frequentist CI says. The Bayesian credible interval CAN be read that way, but requires committing to a prior.
